title: Hanging Drywall
short_answer: Board goes on after framing is true, backing is in, and MEP rough-in is done. Ceiling first, then walls. Stagger joints and land every edge on framing or backing.
summary: Hanging decides how much finishing there is. Every joint you avoid creating is a joint nobody has to tape, coat three times, sand, and touch up.
when_to_use: Framing status is Done and backing for cabinets, grab bars, and TV mounts is in
MEP rough-in and inspections that must precede board are complete
You are ready to place ceiling then wall board
prerequisites: Blocking and backing installed where finishes need them
Ceiling height and openings verified against drawings
plain_words: Use the longest sheets that fit, ceilings before walls, top sheet before bottom, and never let a joint land on the corner of a door. Set the screws so they dimple the paper without tearing it. Fewer seams is the whole game — the finishers inherit whatever you leave them.

materials.name: Gypsum board (type per schedule — Regular / Type X / MR / abuse)

steps.body: Framing accepted: plumb, straight, backing in, no protruding fasteners, no twisted studs.
MEP rough-in complete and inspected. Board over uninspected rough-in comes back off.
Insulation in where it belongs behind the board.
Confirm board type per wall — thickness, rated vs. non-rated, moisture/abuse-resistant, layer count.
Confirm fastener type and spacing for each condition from the spec.
Cut for a snug fit, but don't force a sheet in — forced board bows, breaks at the corners, and pushes framing out of plane.
Push tight to the neighbor before fastening. Gaps mean more mud.
Fasten from the center outward, holding the board tight as you go. Edges-first traps a belly in the middle.
Set gun depth so the head dimples the paper without breaking it. A broken-paper screw holds nothing.
Keep fasteners back from the edges per spec — too close and the edge crumbles.
Leave the specified gap at the floor so board isn't wicking off the slab and isn't bearing.
Walk it with a knife and a gun. Every screw set, none proud, none broken through.
Gaps within tolerance; oversized gaps pre-filled, not left for tape.
All openings cut, none missed, none oversized.
Control joints where the detail shows them, with the board actually broken.
Rated walls photographed, layer one before layer two.

warnings.title: Paper tear at screw heads
warnings.body: A torn face-paper crater will telegraph through finish. Back the screw out and reset beside it; do not mud over a torn crater as if it were a dimple.

warnings.title: Wrong board type
warnings.body: Type X, MR, and abuse board are not interchangeable with regular. Match the schedule — especially at rated assemblies and wet areas.

variations.title: High or awkward ceilings
variations.when: Ceilings above comfortable reach or over stairs
changes: Use a lift or staged scaffolding

variations.title: Fire-rated assemblies
variations.when: Drawings call Type X / UL assembly
changes: Board type and layer count are load-bearing for the rating
Layer orientation and fastener pattern follow the listed assembly

quality_checks.prompt: Every board edge lands on framing or backing
Butt joints staggered — not stacked with ceiling joints
~1/2" gap at floor; board not sitting in the finish
Screw heads dimpled, face paper intact

common_mistakes.title: Floating butt joints
common_mistakes.wrong: Butt joint mid-bay with no backing
common_mistakes.right: Add backing or land on a stud before fastening
common_mistakes.why: Finish will crack at the unsupported joint

common_mistakes.title: Stacked joints
common_mistakes.wrong: Wall butt directly under ceiling butt
common_mistakes.right: Offset joints so planes do not share a weak line
common_mistakes.why: Shared weak line telegraphs and cracks

troubleshooting.symptom: Board won't sit flat / rocks on a stud
troubleshooting.fix: True the framing or shim/plane the box before forcing the board
